topic: Unveiling High-Dimensional Spheres: The Geometry of N-Dimensions

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Building Dimensions
lecture_lines: We build dimensions from 1D, to 2D, to 3D.
The algebraic form grows with each new dimension.
An n-sphere exists in n+1 dimensional space.
animations: Create a dot representing a 0D point (#FFFFFF).
Create a line representing a 1D segment (#FF5733).
Create a circle representing a 2D manifold (#33FF57).

sections.title: Defining the N-Sphere
lecture_lines: An n-sphere is points at constant distance r.
We define spheres based on their surface manifold.

sections.title: The Paradox of Volume and Surface Area
lecture_lines: High-dimensional volume behaves in counter-intuitive ways.
Volume concentrates near the equator as n increases.
Total volume tends toward zero as n grows.
Almost all fruit hides in the outer layer.
animations: Display large sphere with center dot (#FF5733).
Scale sphere while keeping outer shell distinct (#33FF57).
Highlight outer volume with semi-transparent color (#3357FF).
Flash all elements simultaneously for emphasis (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Visualizing the Un-visualizable
lecture_lines: We use orthogonal projections to visualize 4D objects.
A 4D sphere slices through our 3D reality.
It appears, grows, peaks, and then vanishes.
animations: Scale cross-section from zero to max to zero (#3357FF).

sections.title: Applications: Data Science and Beyond
lecture_lines: High-dimensional geometry aids modern machine learning.
The curse of dimensionality makes data points sparse.
Finding patterns becomes harder in higher dimensions.
animations: Animate contraction of axes toward 2D plane (#3357FF).
